Article Title: ‘Ridiculed for eating beef’ at school, 16-year-old Tamil Nadu boy dies by suicide
Article Text:
The Class XI student’s parents at Peelamedu police station

Poll Vote & Share your view What is the most effective measure to prevent caste-based harassment in schools? COIMBATORE: A Class XI Scheduled Caste student of a govt-aided school died by suicide at his residence at Peelamedu in the city on Wednesday allegedly following harassment by his two classmates and a teacher over eating beef.The Peelamedu police have registered a case against class teacher Vijayakumar , headmaster Arun Kumar , and two students of Shri K K Naidu Higher Secondary School on Avinashi Road near Peelamedu in Coimbatore on charges of abetment of suicide and other offences.Police identified the deceased student as A Akilan, 16, son of Ashok Kumar and Kousalya Devi. Kumar works as a laundry manager at a resort in Munnar; Kousalya is a domestic help.Returning home from work around 1pm on Wednesday, Kousalya found her son hanging from the bedroom ceiling. She informed police, who shifted the body to ESI Govt Medical College Hospital for postmortem.In her complaint to police, Kousalya said a few months ago her son’s class teacher, while enrolling Scheduled Caste students for a scholarship scheme, asked who all in the class ate beef.Akilan and another student stood up. After that, two of his classmates started harassing Akilan by mentioning his caste; they also assaulted him, she said, accusing the teacher and headmaster of not taking action after Akilan complained to them.Police registered a case under sections 115(2), 108 of BNS and 3(2)(v) of The Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act and began an investigation.Parents and relatives of Akilan protested in front of the police station on Wednesday evening demanding a proper investigation and the arrest of the teacher and the headmaster. Till Thursday night, the body was not handed over to the family as the postmortem was not conducted.“He (Akilan) wanted to become an advocate. The school management and the teacher are responsible for my son’s death. We need justice for him,” Kumar said.Deputy commissioner of police Thangadurai said an inquiry is underway at the police commissioner level. The Child Welfare Committee is also inquiring.
Article Summary: A Class XI Scheduled Caste student of a govt-aided school died by suicide at his residence at Peelamedu in the city on Wednesday. Police have registered a case against class teacher Vijayakumar, headmaster Arun Kumar and two students of Shri K K Naidu Higher Secondary School.

Article Title: Bihar MLC polls: 5.32 lakh voters to decide fate of 150 candidates across 8 seats, JD(U) rift adds intrigue
Article Text:
Polling began at 8 am today for eight seats in the Bihar Legislative Council (Representative image)





PATNA: Polling for biennial elections to eight Bihar Legislative Council seats began at 8 am on Friday amid tight security, with 5.32 lakh voters eligible to decide the fate of 150 candidates, officials said.Voting will continue till 4 pm for four Graduates and four Teachers constituencies, they said.The combined electorate stands at 5,32,847, including 1,46,611 women and 37 third-gender voters, across 933 polling stations. Counting of votes will take place on October 27.The contest in the Patna Graduates constituency has drawn attention following an open rift within the JD(U), with Mokama MLA Anant Singh backing Jan Suraaj Party candidate Anuj Singh against his own party's nominee, Neeraj Kumar.Kumar, a former minister and a close aide of former chief minister Nitish Kumar, is seeking a fourth consecutive term from the seat.Anant Singh has extended support to Anuj Singh, alleging that Neeraj Kumar had worked against him during last year's assembly elections.Apart from Patna Graduates, the other constituencies going to polls are Darbhanga Graduates, Tirhut Graduates, Kosi Graduates, Patna Teachers, Darbhanga Teachers, Tirhut Teachers and Saran Teachers.The terms of the sitting MLCs are due to expire on November 16.The BJP has fielded candidates in four constituencies, including three sitting MLCs seeking re-election, while the JD(U) has nominated candidates for the remaining four seats.The BJP nominees are MLCs Nawal Kishor Yadav, NK Yadav and Sarvesh Kumar, who are seeking re-election from Patna Teachers, Kosi Graduates and Tirhut Graduates, respectively.The party has also fielded Narendra Kumar Singh from Tirhut Teachers, a seat currently held by Sanjay Kumar Singh of the CPI, a constituent of the opposition INDIA bloc.The Jan Suraaj Party (JSP), led by Prashant Kishor, is contesting all eight seats. The party revised its candidate list after its initial announcement, replacing Bhushan Jha with Shyam Nandan Yadav in Tirhut Teachers and Ravindra Yadav with Mohammad Imtiyaz (Noorani) in Darbhanga Graduates.(With PTI inputs)
Article Summary: Voting will continue till 4 pm for four Graduates and four Teachers constituencies. The combined electorate stands at 5,32,847, including 1,46,611 women and 37 third-gender voters. Counting of votes will take place on October 27.

Article Title: 'No political family faced as much injustice': Akhilesh meets jailed Azam Khan, targets BJP
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav on Thursday met jailed party leader Azam Khan at Rampur district jail and alleged that no political family had faced as much injustice as Khan's family. The meeting comes ahead of the 2027 Uttar Pradesh assembly elections, with the SP discussing its electoral strategy.According to PTI, Yadav accused the BJP government of pursuing political vendetta against Khan and lodging false cases against him."No political family has faced as much injustice as Azam Khan's family," Yadav said while addressing reporters after the hour-long meeting.Yadav said he had discussed all 403 Assembly constituencies with Khan, along with suggestions received from the party's alliance partners. Asked who would contest from Rampur, he declined to reveal the name, saying, "Why should we reveal that now?"Khan and his son, Abdullah Azam Khan, were sentenced to seven years in prison by a Rampur court in November 2025 in dual PAN card cases linked to discrepancies in their dates of birth. Khan has also faced convictions in several other cases, including hate speech and a fake birth certificate case. He has challenged convictions through appeals.Yadav also accused the BJP government of undermining the Mohammad Ali Jauhar University, an institution associated with Khan, alleging that a conspiracy had been hatched to destroy it.He said, "The dream Azam Khan had for the university, for education and for building the future of young people, will be fulfilled by Samajwadi Party workers."Invoking the idea of Ram Rajya, Yadav alleged that justice and fairness were being undermined in Rampur. "False cases do not have the strength to keep the truth imprisoned. It may take time, there may be some delay, but the truth cannot be held captive in false cases," he said.The SP chief said defeating the BJP remained his party's primary objective ahead of the 2027 Assembly elections. He also reiterated the party's allegations of electoral malpractice in the 2022 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections.Asked about Khan's health, Yadav said it was better but added that the difficulties associated with being in jail remained. Yadav was also scheduled to visit Khan's residence and meet his family members later on Thursday.
Article Summary: Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav met jailed party leader Azam Khan at Rampur district jail. The meeting comes ahead of the 2027 Uttar Pradesh assembly elections, with the SP discussing its electoral strategy. Yadav accused the BJP government of pursuing political vendetta against Khan and lodging false cases.

Article Title: CJP leaders Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka seek more time, skip Delhi Police questioning
Article Text:
Delhi Police Crime Branch has summoned CJP leaders Sourav Das and Ashutosh Ranka to its Rajouri Garden office

NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka will not appear before the Delhi Police Crime Branch for questioning on Thursday after seeking more time, sources told ANI. Police are expected to issue a fresh notice to the two leaders, the sources said.The Crime Branch had summoned Das and Ranka to its Rajouri Garden office on Thursday, a day after they were released from judicial custody.The two were released after a Special Executive Magistrate (SEM) court accepted their personal and surety bonds and recorded their written undertakings to maintain peace and abide by the law.SEM Ritu Raj directed them to furnish personal and surety bonds of Rs 50,000 each until the conclusion of the enquiry. They were also instructed to appear on every hearing date and comply with the conditions specified in their bonds and undertakings.In their written undertakings, the leaders promised not to breach peace or disturb public tranquillity. They also agreed not to call for protests at Jantar Mantar until the site is denotified in accordance with the law, and said any future demonstrations would be held within the constitutional framework.The two leaders were detained in connection with an October 13 protest at Jantar Mantar, which had been denotified as a designated protest site. Police alleged that they entered the area through private premises and violated conditions related to maintaining peace.The Delhi Police had earlier sought a further three-day extension of their judicial custody, citing concerns over a possible breach of peace and law and order. Police also pointed to alleged differences between statements made by the leaders before the court and their subsequent remarks to the media.The matter is scheduled for further proceedings before the SEM court on October 23 at 3 pm. Das, Ranka and their sureties have been directed to remain present.
Article Summary: Delhi Police Crime Branch has summoned CJP leaders Sourav Das and Ashutosh Ranka to its Rajouri Garden office. Police are expected to issue a fresh notice to the two leaders, the sources said. The two were released after a Special Executive Magistrate (SEM) court accepted their personal and surety bonds.

Article Title: 'They have the right to protest, argue': Ex-BJP leader Annamalai questions govt's handling of CJP protests
Article Text:
‘I disagree with CJP’s protest strategies’

NEW DELHI: Former Tamil Nadu BJP chief K Annamalai has questioned the Centre over its handling of protests by the CJP group in Delhi, raising concerns over restrictions at Jantar Mantar, preventive detention and bail proceedings involving its office-bearers.In a series of posts, former BJP leader K Annamalai invoked then-Gujarat CM Narendra Modi’s 2011 remarks condemning the police crackdown on an anti-corruption protest at Delhi’s Ramlila Maidan, questioning whether the principles Modi defended then applied to protesters today.“In 2011, the then Gujarat chief minister, Narendra Modi, said that if his hands had not been tied, he would have gone to Delhi and revolted against the central government,” Annamalai wrote.“In my view, what the honourable Prime Minister Narendra Modi said then was absolutely right. There was nothing wrong with it,” he added.Annamalai, who said he left the BJP on June 5, 2026, questioned how Jantar Mantar was removed as a designated protest site after CJP sought permission to hold a demonstration.He also raised concerns over an assistant commissioner of police (ACP) functioning as a special executive magistrate with the authority to decide whether a person should remain in preventive detention.“In the CJP case, Delhi Police itself is the complainant, while an ACP belonging to the same Delhi Police force has the authority to decide whether the accused should remain in preventive detention,” he said.He also questioned why eight bail sureties had been rejected and why a magistrate had cross-examined a person offering bail surety. Annamalai further asked whether action had been taken over the alleged use of pellet guns and other standard operating procedure violations during protests against the NEET examination.Comparing the situation with protests during previous Congress and Aam Aadmi Party governments in Delhi, he asked how BJP workers who allegedly jumped barricades or disobeyed police orders had been treated.“Was it anything like what is happening now? Certainly not!” he said.Annamalai said he disagreed with CJP’s approach but defended its right to protest.“As I said yesterday, I do not agree with CJP’s protest strategies, and I believe many of its approaches are misguided,” he said.“But if you ask me whether they have the right to protest, argue and fight for an issue they consider important, my answer is an unequivocal yes!” he added.He also criticised the tendency to portray protests against the Union government as anti-national or foreign-funded.“It is genuinely exhausting and frustrating to see every protest against the central government and every statement it issues being portrayed as an anti-national act funded by foreign powers,” he said.Annamalai further questioned whether the BJP was inadvertently giving CJP publicity by targeting it, referring to a Dussehra event led by BJP MLA Ashok Goyal.“Is the BJP genuinely opposed to CJP, or is it giving the organisation free publicity?” he asked.The remarks come days after CJP leaders Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das were arrested over an alleged attempt to trespass at Jantar Mantar, which had been de-notified as a designated protest site. They were sent to Tihar Jail and later released after signing a bond.
Article Summary: Former Tamil Nadu BJP chief K Annamalai has questioned the Centre over its handling of protests by the CJP group in Delhi. He has raised concerns over restrictions at Jantar Mantar, preventive detention and bail proceedings involving its office-bearers. He also questioned whether the BJP was inadvertently giving CJP publicity by targeting it.

Article Title: 'You want to protect infiltrators' votes': Amit Shah's sharp attack on Rahul Gandhi over 'vote theft' claims
Article Text:

‘Yamuna will be cleaned by May 2029’

NEW DELHI: Union home minister Amit Shah on Thursday hit out at leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi over his allegations of “vote chori” and "collusion" between the Election Commission and the BJP , accusing the Congress of using the issue to explain its electoral defeats.Addressing an event in Delhi on his birthday where he launched projects worth Rs 8,941 crore for cleaning the Yamuna, Shah also targeted the Arvind Kejriwal-led Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) over its governance in Delhi and Punjab.“The BJP keeps winning elections, and the opposition is troubled by it. That is why they have come up with the excuse of ‘vote chori’, or vote theft,” Shah said.“Rahul ji, you keep talking about vote theft because you want to protect the votes of infiltrators,” he added.Union home minister argued that the BJP had been winning elections in several states even before Narendra Modi became prime minister, while the Congress had remained out of power in many states for decades.“Congress, its allies accuse BJP of vote theft but are out of power in many states for decades,” he said.Referring to the Congress's electoral record, Shah cited its prolonged absence from power in several states and questioned whether its electoral setbacks had begun only after Modi became prime minister.“When I say the BJP will remain in power for 30 years, they accuse us of stealing votes. They ask how Amit Shah knows the election results in advance. Amit Shah was born here, lives here and will die here. I do not have to travel abroad every six months. I live among the people of this country,” he said.Attacking Lok Sabha LoP he said, "When court rulings favour you, you call them fair, but when they go against you, you question them. These double standards will not work, Rahul ji."Shah also targeted Rahul over opposition protests in Delhi, saying, “You cannot overturn the people's mandate through political manoeuvres and mob pressure. Winning elections is not about staging protests and sit-ins.”Shah also accused previous governments in Delhi of failing to prevent untreated sewage from entering the Yamuna and said the BJP government was committed to cleaning the river.“Congress, AAP govts allowed discharge of sewer water in Yamuna; we will clean it by May 2029,” Shah said.The projects launched at the event are aimed at improving sewage treatment and wastewater management, expanding sewer connections and reducing pollution in the river.Turning to poll-bound Punjab, where the AAP government is led by chief minister Bhagwant Mann, Shah attacked the ruling party over the drug menace and expressed confidence that the NDA would come to power in the state.“Drug menace prevalent in Punjab; people of state want NDA government,” he said.“AAP is going to be routed in Punjab elections , we will end drug trafficking in state,” Shah added.
Article Summary: Union home minister Amit Shah hit out at leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi. He accused the Congress of using the issue to explain its electoral defeats. Shah also targeted the Arvind Kejriwal-led Aam Aadmi Party over its governance in Delhi and Punjab.

Article Title: INDIA bloc huddle: Leaders to meet virtually on CEC row; SIR irregularities on agenda
Article Text:
INDIA bloc leaders to meet today to discuss strategy against CEC Gyanesh Kumar

Opposition steps up campaign against Election Commission

Kharge targets immunity law, EVMs

INDIA bloc challenges SIR, Jantar Mantar decision

NEW DELHI: Leaders of the INDIA bloc will meet through video conferencing on Thursday evening to discuss their strategy over the ongoing row involving chief election commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar, sources cited by news agency ANI said, with Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge set to chair the meeting.The meeting comes as Opposition parties continue their campaign against alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and demand accountability from the Election Commission of India (ECI).The opposition has accused the poll panel of facilitating the deletion of eligible voters from electoral rolls and has sought Kumar’s resignation.The Election Commission has maintained that it follows established procedures and defended its role in conducting elections.The INDIA bloc had earlier announced a joint action plan under its “Save Democracy” campaign. The proposed programme included protests, a march towards the Election Commission headquarters and a rally in New Delhi on November 1.On October 6, INDIA bloc MPs led by Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi marched towards Nirvachan Sadan, the Election Commission’s headquarters, seeking a meeting with the poll panel.Delhi Police stopped the march amid heavy barricading and detained several opposition leaders, including Rahul Gandhi and Congress MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra. They were later released.Following the protest, the ECI said Delhi Police had informed it that a delegation of around 240 MPs wanted to meet the Election Commissioners and submit a memorandum at the Parliament House Annexe.The poll panel described the proposed venue and manner of seeking the meeting as “unusual” under its established protocol.Delhi Police said the march had not been granted permission and cited prohibitory orders to explain its action against the protesters.The opposition subsequently approached President Droupadi Murmu. An INDIA bloc delegation, including Rahul Gandhi, Kharge, Trinamool Congress chief Mamata Banerjee and Samajwadi Party representatives, submitted a memorandum outlining its demands on October 9.The memorandum sought Kumar’s resignation, suspension of the SIR exercise, restoration of voters allegedly deleted from electoral rolls and a return to paper ballots.The opposition also called for the repeal of the 2023 law granting immunity to the chief election commissioner and other election commissioners for official duties.On Wednesday, Kharge accused the BJP-led government of undermining democratic institutions and shielding election officials from accountability. He said the opposition’s campaign was aimed at protecting the Constitution and democracy rather than securing electoral gains for any particular party.Kharge criticised Section 16 of the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners Act, 2023, which grants legal immunity to current and former Election Commissioners for official duties.He argued that the provision protected election officials from accountability and demanded its repeal.“We are asking the BJP to repeal that law. Because you are giving protection to the Election Commissioner and letting him make mistakes. And whatever mistakes have happened today, they happened through Gyanesh Kumar. Why did you give him immunity? It was given so that you can make mistakes through him just by telling him to do so, and forgive him. The Chief Justice doesn’t have immunity. The President of India doesn’t have it. An Election Commissioner does,” Kharge said.He also called for Kumar’s removal, the scrapping of electronic voting machines (EVMs) and a return to paper ballots, while demanding stricter checks on changes to voter lists.“Follow the constitutional system, and remove Gyanesh Kumar, whom you have appointed today. Along with removing him, change the system too. Bring the previous law back, get rid of the EVMs, bring back ballot papers, and the software that sits in one place and controls the whole country. Stop using BLOs to make changes to the voter list,” he said.Kharge also criticised the government’s response to opposition concerns, alleging that Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union home minister Amit Shah were using ministers and constitutional officials to avoid directly addressing the issues raised by the opposition.At a meeting on October 13, INDIA bloc leaders reiterated their resolve to continue the campaign and said they would challenge the denotification of Jantar Mantar as a designated protest site.Opposition leaders, including Rahul Gandhi and Kharge, have also approached the Supreme Court challenging aspects of the SIR exercise.On October 15, the Supreme Court issued notices to the Election Commission, Kumar and Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi on petitions challenging aspects of the revision exercise.The court also agreed to examine the denotification of Jantar Mantar and directed Delhi Police to preserve CCTV footage of the protests amid allegations of excessive force.Thursday’s meeting is expected to focus on the opposition’s strategy in the continuing dispute with the Election Commission, including its demands over the SIR exercise and accountability of the poll panel.
Article Summary: Leaders of the INDIA bloc will meet through video conferencing on Thursday evening. Meeting comes as Opposition parties continue their campaign against alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. Opposition has accused the poll panel of facilitating the deletion of eligible voters from electoral rolls and has sought Kumar’s resignation.

NEW DELHI: The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke in another X post on Monday claimed that the local Deputy Commissioner of Police (DCP) in his hometown had “suddenly gone on leave” and that a new officer had been brought in to take charge.Dipke’s remarks came amid party's earlier claim that he and fellow CJP leaders Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Dass could be arrested before October 10 under the National Security Act (NSA) or other provisions.AISA national president Neha Bora on Monday claimed that protesting journalists have been detained at the Delhi Cantonment Police Station.In a post on X, Neha said "Rosy and other protesting journalists are detained at Delhi Cantt PS. Trinamool Congress (TMC) MP Derek O’Brien also extended support to Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leaders as party spokesperson Ashutosh Ranka claimed that multiple sources had warned that the three could be arrested before October 10 under the National Security Act (NSA) or other equivalent provisions.“With you all the way 🪳🪳stay strong. ‘10 Oct poora desh aa raha hai…’,” O’Brien said in a post on X while replying to Dipke.CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke reacting to the claim said they would not be intimidated by the possibility of action under laws such as the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA) or National Security Act (NSA).“If the Govt believes that the threat of UAPA, NSA or years behind bars will scare us into silence, it won’t,” Dipke said in a post on X, adding that the protesters were prepared to spend “months or years in jail” but would not back down from their campaign to “save democracy”.He further said that they follow the path shown by Mahatma Gandhi and continue to resist “peacefully and non-violently”, despite what he described as attempts by the state to intimidate them.The developments come amid the CJP-led campaign against the Election Commission’s Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. The protesters have been demanding accountability from chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over the exercise and have announced further mobilisation on October 10 in Delhi.
Article Summary: AISA national president Neha Bora claims that protesting journalists have been detained at the Delhi Cantonment Police Station. CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke reacting to the claim said they would not be intimidated by the possibility of action under laws such as the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act.

Article Title: ‘Do you eat beef’: Coimbatore teacher under scanner after Dalit Class XI student dies by suicide
Article Text:
Peelamedu police have registered a case involving a teacher, headmaster, and two students related to a student’s suicide





COIMBATORE: Peelamedu police in the city have registered a case under three sections against four people, including two students of a government-aided school, in connection with the suicide of a Scheduled Caste student near Peelamedu.A. Akilan, 16, was a Class XI student of a government-aided school (KK Naidu) near Peelamedu. Article Title: Manoj Jarange drops audio clip alleging plot to weaken Maratha quota stir, sparks political storm and demand for probe
Article Text:
Manoj Jarange released an audio clip claiming he was offered Rs 500 crore to stop his protest.

(With inputs from PTI)





CHHATRAPATI SAMBHAJINAGAR: Maratha quota activist Manoj Jarange on Thursday released about 10 minutes of a 32-minute audio clip alleging a Rs 500-crore payment to him to call off his agitation, claiming it was part of a conspiracy to weaken the reservation movement. The clip sparked a political controversy, with both opposition and Mahayuti members demanding a thorough probe.After raising the issue at his Dasara rally in Beed, Jarange played the part of the audio clip at a news conference in Ambad tehsil in Jalna on Thursday and demanded a probe. In the clip, a woman allegedly claimed that Rs 500 crore had reached Jarange. The discussion then shifted to Jarange’s rising political clout, efforts to blunt his agitation and plans to rally Maratha leaders against him.Jarange described the recording as an evidence of a conspiracy to weaken the Maratha reservation movement and alleged sustained attempts over the past three years to discredit him. He urged Prime Minister Narendra Modi , chief minister Devendra Fadnavis and deputy CM Eknath Shinde to order an investigation. He also threatened further disclosures if the alleged conspiracy continued.Shiv Sena members demanded a forensic examination of the audio clip. Industries minister Uday Samant said voice samples must be sent to a forensic laboratory to verify their authenticity.He also called for an investigation into who recorded and circulated the clip, and with what intent.Former minister Ramdas Kadam questioned why Jarange had withheld the recording for two years, claiming it dated back to Oct 14, 2024. Sena MP Naresh Mhaske urged Jarange to submit the clip to police and the cyber cell, saying the identities of those heard in the clip must be verified.Terming the audio clip put out by Jarange absolutely fake, IT minister Ashish Shelar also sought an inquiry into the clip’s origins and authenticity. “How it was leaked....how did it reach Jarange and why has he brought it out now... There should be a thorough inquiry,” he said. BJP spokesperson Navnath Ban suggested it could be AI-generated.State minister Chandrashekhar Bawankule said Jarange should file a complaint over his allegation about payment of Rs 500 crore, assuring a “thorough and impartial” probe if evidence was submitted. Talking to reporters over the issue in Jalna, Bawankule said, “If Jarange has concrete evidence regarding the alleged Rs 500 crore payment (as mentioned in the) audio clip and the conspiracy to implicate him, he should register an official complaint with the police or the district collector instead of speaking only to the media. ”Meanwhile, Maharashtra Congress chief Harshwardhan Sapkal demanded an Enforcement Directorate investigation into the alleged money trail.On Wednesday, deputy CM Shinde, speaking with reporters in New Delhi, had dared Jarange to prove his allegation regarding payment of Rs 500 crore. Talking to reporters, Shinde had said no one had been paid (or had received) Rs 500 crore. “He (Jarange) should have verified facts before speaking. He should furnish proof to the agencies concerned and this matter should be probed,” Shinde said.
Article Summary: Maratha quota activist Manoj Jarange released about 10 minutes of a 32-minute audio clip alleging a Rs 500-crore payment to him to call off his agitation. Jarange claimed it was part of a conspiracy to weaken the reservation movement. The clip sparked a political controversy, with both opposition and Mahayuti members demanding a thorough probe.

Article Title: Tough fight between two factions of NCP on cards as stage set for MLC polls
Article Text:
Election machinery was in action mode on the eve of MLC poll on Thursday

Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar





: The stage is set for polling in the Aurangabad division graduates’ constituency on Friday, where 3,26,701 graduate voters will decide the fate of 41 candidates across 842 polling centres in eight districts. Polling will be held from 8 am to 4 pm, with the counting scheduled for Oct 27.While political equations have turned messy across both Mahayuti and Maha Vikas Aghadi (MVA) camps, the two factions of Nationalist Congress Party (NCP) are largely battling this election as a fight for legacy. The contest is expected to be a direct fight between sitting MLC Satish Chavan of NCP and Pratapsinh Patil of NCP (SP).Within Mahayuti alliance, Sillod Shiv Sena MLA Abdul Sattar campaigned against Chavan, with a few prominent party leaders allegedly siding with Sattar secretly. MVA also faced an internal split after its alliance partner, Shiv Sena (UBT), fielded Dilip Ghuge.Graduate voters will cast their ballots through a preferential voting system, which differs from general elections. Voters must use only the violet sketch pen supplied by the polling officer. Using any other pen, ballpoint, or pencil will invalidate the ballot paper.“Voters must write ‘1’ in the preference column next to the candidate of their choice.The figure ‘1’ must appear against only one candidate. Voters can then mark further preferences as 2, 3, or 4 against other contestants in order of choice,” election authorities said. Preferences must be indicated in figures only—such as 1, 2, 3; I, II, III; or १, २, ३ (in Devanagari script)—and not written in words.“Do not put tick marks or crosses, and do not write your name, initials, signature, or leave a thumb impression. A ballot where ‘1’ is not marked, or where ‘1’ is marked against more than one candidate, will be rejected,” said divisional commissioner of Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar and returning officer, G Sreekanth.Sreekanth also reviewed the election preparedness across Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, Jalna, Beed, Latur, Dharashiv, Parbhani, Nanded, and Hingoli districts. The review covered basic amenities at polling stations, voter facilitation, availability of polling material, staff deployment, and security arrangements, alongside planning for party booths outside polling centres and safe transportation of ballot boxes.
Article Summary: 3,26,701 graduate voters will decide the fate of 41 candidates across 842 polling centres in eight districts. Political equations have turned messy across both Mahayuti and Maha Vikas Aghadi (MVA) camps. Two factions of Nationalist Congress Party (NCP) are largely battling this election as a fight for legacy.

Article Title: Crackdown on water wastage, illegal taps in Sambhajinagar
Article Text:
Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar

:





Stepping up its campaign against water theft and wastage, Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar Municipal Corporation has begun imposing spot fines, disconnecting illegal tap connections and warning of criminal action against violators.A special squad on Wednesday fined three consumers a total of Rs 25,000 after finding drinking water being wasted at a hotel on Railway Station Road and a commercial complex in Osmanpura.“Every citizen is entitled to their rightful share of water. Water wastage and illegal connections will not be tolerated. Those using unauthorised connections should regularise them immediately or face penal and police action,” Yedge said.To intensify enforcement, the civic body also conducted a special training programme for its staff under the guidance of municipal commissioner G Sreekanth Yedge and additional commissioner Kalpita Pimple.Wednesday’s action follows an earlier inspection in Asefia Colony, where officials found treated water flowing onto the road. Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar Municipal Corporation (CSMC) disconnected 39 unauthorised tap connections and imposed Rs 5,000 fine.
Article Summary: Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar Municipal Corporation has begun imposing spot fines, disconnecting illegal tap connections and warning of criminal action against violators. A special squad on Wednesday fined three consumers a total of Rs 25,000 after finding drinking water being wasted at a hotel and a commercial complex.

Article Title: Violet pens and numerical rankings: ERO issues guidelines for valid ballot voting in MLC polls
Article Text:
Poll booth staffers assigned for MLC polls in Solapur left with jumbo ballot box and other material to their respective polling booths

Kolhapur

:





As many as 3.88 lakh voters are eligible to vote in the graduates’ constituency, while 61,940 voters are registered for the teachers’ constituency in the MLC elections.Voting will be conducted via ballot paper, and voters must mark their preferences numerically. Election authorities and candidates alike are actively raising awareness on how to cast a valid vote, given that these elections typically witness a high number of invalid ballots. In the last election alone, more than 10,000 votes were declared invalid in the graduates’ constituency.Sheetal Teli-Ugale, the election returning officer (ERO) and divisional commissioner, appealed to first-time voters to thoroughly understand the voting process. “A violet sketch pen will be provided at the booths; no other pen will be allowed to mark preferences. Preference numbers must not be written in words; they must be entered as 1, 2, 3 or in Roman numerals within the box next to the candidate’s name. No tick marks are allowed. No two candidates can be given the same preference number, or else the ballot will be deemed invalid,” the ERO stated.Voting will take place from 8 am to 4 pm. Voters who have not received their EPIC slips can use any of the 10 valid alternative documents as identity proof.According to the final electoral roll for the graduates’ constituency, Pune district has 88,202 voters, Satara has 47,463, Solapur has 49,072, Sangli has 88,070, and Kolhapur has the highest share with 1,14,562 voters. For the teachers’ constituency, Pune has registered 16,822 voters, Solapur 15,303, Satara 9,454, Sangli 8,062, and Kolhapur 12,299.In the Pune graduates’ seat, the contest is largely a direct fight between BJP’s Smita Jadhav and NCP (SP) candidate Harshada Deshmukh Jadhav. Meanwhile, the teachers’ seat is witnessing a multi-cornered contest, with Kaustubh Gavade of BJP and Jayant Asgaonkar of Congress serving as the primary contenders. Shiv Sena has extended its support to independent candidate Sachin Sanap, who could act as a spoiler for BJP. The counting of votes will take place at Balewadi Stadium on Oct 27.NCP (SP) president Sharad Pawar issued a video message appealing to citizens to vote for Maha Vikas Aghadi (MVA) candidates. Concurrently, chief minister Devendra Fadnavis spearheaded rallies for BJP and reached out to disgruntled Shiv Sena leaders in Satara to consolidate support for the party’s nominees.
Article Summary: As many as 3.88 lakh voters are eligible to vote in the graduates' constituency. 61,940 voters are registered for the teachers' constituency in the MLC elections. In the last election alone, more than 10,000 votes were declared invalid.

Article Title: Sangli DCC Bank poll: 19 elected unopposed
Article Text:
Kolhapur:





Setting aside their political rivalry, politicians of Mahayuti and MVA camps struck a rare deal for Sangli District Central Cooperative (DCC) Bank elections, resulting in 19 of the 21 seats being won unopposed on the final day for withdrawal of nominations.The unprecedented understanding between the two camps effectively turned the contest into a consensus election, leaving only two seats headed for polling on Nov 1. One seat is being contested by BJP MLA Gopichand Padalkar and the other by former MLA and NCP leader Ajitrao Ghorpade.As per the seat-sharing arrangement, seven are with NCP (SP) nominees, six with Congress, four with BJP, three with Shiv Sena and one is with NCP.The agreement comes despite strained political relations between the two alliances and was justified as a response to the severe drought prevailing in Sangli district.BJP functionary Prithviraj Deshmukh said chief minister Devendra Fadnavis had urged politicians to avoid a prolonged election battle and focus administrative and political attention on drought relief.“During a recent meeting at Kolhapur airport, chief minister Devendra Fadnavis urged Mahayuti politicians to avoid a divisive election battle amid the worsening drought.While Mahayuti was fully prepared for the contest, he said drought relief should take precedence and assured us he would speak to NCP (SP) functionary Jayant Patil and Congress neta Vishwajeet Kadam. After separate discussions, a consensus emerged, and Jayant Patil responded positively, paving the way for the maximum number of candidates to be elected unopposed,” Deshmukh said at a joint news conference of Mahayuti and MVA leaders.NCP (SP) politician Jayant Patil said the bank’s interests had been placed above party politics. “We have worked together before. This election is about the future of the bank, not political parties,” he said.The outcome also underlined the continuing dominance of influential political families in Sangli’s cooperative sector. Several candidates elected unopposed are either senior politicians themselves or close relatives of influential netas across party lines.Among them are sitting MLA Vishwajeet Kadam; Amol Babar, brother of Shiv Sena MLA Suhas Babar; Mahendra Lad, a relative of Kadam; Devraj Patil, a relative of Jayant Patil; Viraj Naik, son of outgoing chairman and former MLA Mansingrao Naik; former MLA Sumantai Patil, mother of NCP (SP) MLA Rohit R.R. Patil; Puja Patil, wife of Sangli MP Vishal Patil; and Varsha Sawant, wife of former MLA Vikram Sawant.
Article Summary: Politicians of Mahayuti and MVA camps struck a rare deal for Sangli District Central Cooperative (DCC) Bank elections. 19 of the 21 seats were won unopposed on the final day for withdrawal of nominations. The unprecedented understanding between the two camps effectively turned the contest into a consensus election.

Article Title: Rs 1 lakh bribe trap: Navi Mumbai ACB catches circle officer, talathi and woman assistant
Article Text:
The arrested accused were identified as Keshav Dagdu Mohite, Jaihind Birsha Koli (49) and Monika Vijnesh Patil (36).





NAVI MUMBAI: The Navi Mumbai Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) has arrested two revenue officials and a woman assistant for allegedly accepting a Rs 1 lakh bribe from a villager in Chirner, Uran taluka, to register the names of his relatives in the 7/12 extract of a land record.The arrested accused were identified as Keshav Dagdu Mohite (52), circle officer at Koproli in Uran taluka; Jaihind Birsha Koli (49), talathi; and Monika Vijnesh Patil (36), an assistant to the revenue officials.Dharmaraj Sonake, deputy superintendent of police, Navi Mumbai ACB, said the complainant had applied to register the names of the heirs of his deceased sister in the 7/12 extract of their land in Chirner.The land was jointly owned by the complainant's maternal uncle, aunt, brother and sister. The complainant had also applied for deletion of his deceased brother's name and submitted the request to circle officer Mohite and talathi Koli. However, the two officials allegedly demanded Rs 1 lakh from him to process the work.Dy SP Sonake said, "After verification of the complaint on Monday, when it was confirmed that the revenue officers Mohite and Koli had told the complainant to hand over the bribe amount to the accused woman assistant Monika Patil, a trap was laid on Tuesday around 2 pm. After the woman assistant Monika Patil accepted the demanded bribe of Rs 1 lakh from the complainant and handed it over to circle officer Keshav Mohite, both were caught red-handed and arrested. While, the acccused Talathi Jaihind Koli who was involved in the bribe demand was taken into custody from Dronagiri."
Article Summary: The Navi Mumbai Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) has arrested two revenue officials and a woman assistant for allegedly accepting a Rs 1 lakh bribe. The arrested accused were identified as Keshav Dagdu Mohite (52), circle officer at Koproli in Uran taluka; Jaihind Birsha Koli (49), talathi; and Monika Vijnesh Patil (36)

Article Title: Man in Mahindra Thar with duplicate plate molests woman, knocks down another in Kharghar
Article Text:
30-year-old man was apprehended for allegedly molesting a woman and injuring another in Navi Mumbai.





NAVI MUMBAI: A 30-year-old man wearing a mask and driving a red Thar SUV with a duplicate registration number plate was apprehended by the Crime Branch Unit-3 team within 10 hours on Thursday evening.He had allegedly molested a 26-year-old woman walking on the street in Kharghar, around 400metres from Pethpada metro station, on September 30 night and, an hour later, severely injured a 22-year-old woman by knocking her down in Belpada, Sector 3, Kharghar.Acting on a complaint by the woman allegedly molested by the Thar SUV driver, Kharghar police registered an FIR under BNS section 74 for the offence of assault or criminal force against a woman with the intent to outrage her modesty.While, as per the complaint by the injured woman Shrawani Dandekar, a resident of sector 3, Belpada, an FIR under relevant BNS sections and Motor Vehicle Act was registered against the Thar SUV driver for rash and negligent driving causing hurt.The detained aaccused identified as Ali alias Talib Ahsan Nakhvi, a resident of sector 50, Seawoods, Nerul was handed over to Kharghar police for further legal action.Previously, in January 2021, he was arrested by Nerul police in the FIR registered against him for alleged kidnapping, sexual harassment and molestation of a woman.Sanjay Joshi, senior inspector of Kharghar said, "The accused Nakhvi has been detained and subsequently it will be decided whether to arrest him or serve with a notice under Bharatiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) for cooperating in police investigating."Audumbar Patil, senior inspector of crime branch unit-3 said, "After an FIR for molestation was registered at Kharghar police station by the victim woman, a resident of sector 34, Kharghar. As per the orders of higher authority, our team started a parallel probe. From the CCTV camera surveillance near the crime scene, we obtained the red Thar SUV's registration number, which was of Vashi RTO passing.""When verified, the registration number was found to be that of a Maruti WagonR car. As the accused had used a duplicate registration number plate, we scrutinized as many as 62 Thar SUVs registered with various Regional Transport Offices (RTOs). Subsequently, we obtained the registration number of a red Thar SUV that was registered with Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar RTO," Patil added.SPI Patil further informed, "The SUV was registered in the name of Ali alias Talib Ahsan Nakhvi, a resident of Devaki Apartment in sector-50, Seawoods. From his mobile number registered with the RTO, his location was tracked.""He was apprehended from Bonkode village, Koparkhairane on Thursday late evening. Upon thorough interrogation, he confessed that he had inappropriately touched the woman pedestrian near Pethpada metro station while he drove his Thar SUV and sped away. He even confessed to have injured a woman pedestrian by hitting her his SUV while driving in Belpada area," he said.
Article Summary: A 30-year-old man wearing a mask and driving a red Thar SUV with a duplicate registration number plate was apprehended by the Crime Branch Unit-3 team on Thursday evening. He had allegedly molested a woman walking on the street in Kharghar, around 400metres from Pethpada metro station, on September 30 night. An hour later, he severely injured a woman by knocking her down in Belpada, Sector 3, KharGHar.

Article Title: 2 women escape from RPF lockup in Navi Mumbai; 1 held after 6 hours, cop suspended
Article Text:
The women removed their sarees, tied one end to the generator on the balcony and climbed down before escaping. (AI image)





NAVI MUMBAI: In a major security lapse at Belapur Railway Protection Force (RPF), two women arrested for allegedly attempting to steal overhead electric wires from the Juinagar railway godown escaped from the lockup after midnight on September 28.One of them was apprehended around six hours later, while the other remains at large.The woman constable on night duty has been suspended and a departmental inquiry has been initiated against her.As per the FIR registered by RPF sub-inspector Milap Parte (52) at Panvel GRP, a case was registered on September 24 under Section 3(a) of the Railway Property (Unauthorized Possession) Act, 1966, Amendment 2012, at Belapur railway police station.The case was based on a written memo submitted by RPF personnel Ravikant Gade regarding the theft of overhead electric wires from the godown at Juinagar railway station on September 21.During the probe, a trap was laid on September 26 and around 1pm, two women were found loitering suspiciously near the Juinagar godown with the alleged intention of committing theft.They were taken into custody and identified as Rupali Kailas Kurhade (30), from Jalna, and Shalibai Ashok Pawar (49), from Bhiwandi.They were arrested after an FIR was registered for attempted theft and produced before a CSMT court, which remanded them to police custody till September 30. They were lodged in the lockup at Belapur RPF police station.Day-shift woman constable Rakhi Malaiya was assigned guard duty at the lockup, after which woman head constable Pooja Bagre was on night duty.Around 2am on September 28, when Bagre had gone to the toilet, the two women allegedly managed to open the lock by inserting their hands through the iron bars of the lockup and jerking it. Police suspect the lock may not have been secured properly.The women then reached the balcony at the rear end of the police station. They removed their sarees, tied one end to the generator on the balcony and climbed down before escaping.The incident was captured on CCTV footage. PSI Parte learnt about the escape after waking up at home around 6.30am and finding several missed calls from head constable Bagre and ASI Rajiv Parsan.Sunil Nila, chief spokesperson of Central Railway, said, "One accused woman Rupali Kurhade was apprehended from near Nerul railway station around 8.45 am. The other accused Shalibai Pawar is still absconding."
Article Summary: The women removed their sarees, tied one end to the generator on the balcony and climbed down before escaping. One of them was apprehended around six hours later, while the other remains at large. The woman constable on night duty has been suspended and a departmental inquiry has been initiated.

Article Title: Ulhasnagar social activist Haresh Gajwani shot dead outside railway station, 3 arrested
Article Text:
Haresh Gajwani was murdered outside Ulhasnagar railway station on Wednesday night.





ULHASNAGAR: Police have arrested three suspects in connection with the murder of social worker Haresh Gajwani, who was shot dead outside Ulhasnagar railway station on Wednesday night. The suspects have been identified as Avinash Naidu, Vijay Singh and Noor Alam Khan.According to preliminary investigations, Gajwani and Naidu had a long-standing dispute. In 2021, counter-cases were registered against the two sides following a dispute, which allegedly contributed to continuing tensions between Gajwani and the accused.Police said the three suspects were traced and detained with the help of CCTV footage. Investigators are examining the alleged past rivalry, along with other possible motives behind the murder.Gajwani, 54, was allegedly attacked by three assailants who fired two rounds at him before fleeing the scene. Locals and police took him to Central Hospital, where doctors declared him "brought dead".Recently, Gajwani had posted on X, tagging senior officials from various police departments, as well as the chief minister, deputy chief minister and FDA commissioner Tukaram Mundhe. In his posts, he had highlighted alleged illegal activities in the area and claimed that some police personnel were supporting those involved. He had also expressed fears for his life, warning that the police personnel he had accused would also be responsible if anything happened to him.
Article Summary: Haresh Gajwani, 54, was shot dead outside Ulhasnagar railway station on Wednesday. Police have arrested three suspects in connection with the murder. The suspects have been identified as Avinash Naidu, Vijay Singh and Noor Alam Khan. Investigators are examining the alleged past rivalry, along with other possible motives.

Article Title: Talegaon plant CEO arrested in CO2 leak case; gets bail
Article Text:
A senior police officer said seven accused had been arrested before Kadam in the case

Pune:

TOI





Schaeffler India chief executive officer and managing director Harsha Kadam was on Thursday formally arrested in connection with the June 9 CO₂ leak at the company’s Talegaon MIDC plant which killed two workers and injured four others. He was later granted bail by a court in Vadgaon Maval.Talegaon MIDC police had detained Kadam in Mumbai on Monday. However, during a medical examination before his production in court for a remand hearing, his blood pressure spiked, following which he was admitted to Sassoon General Hospital.The court directed police to keep Kadam under detention and police guard at the hospital until his discharge and ordered that he be produced before it immediately thereafter.“Kadam was formally arrested after his discharge from hospital and subsequently produced before the court, which granted him bail,” Vijayanand Patil, senior police inspector at Talegaon MIDC police station, toldThe leak occurred on June 9 while expired CO₂ cylinders were being replaced in the fire suppression system at the Talegaon plant. Police initially registered an accidental death case before filing an FIR on July 4, naming six people, including the company’s safety officer and personnel from two contractors engaged for the work.A senior police officer said seven accused had been arrested before Kadam, making him the eighth arrest in the case. “We have already filed a chargesheet in the matter,” the officer said.Explaining the allegations against Kadam, the officer said the CO₂ cylinders had been kept in a basement pit without the necessary permission. Such an installation was not permitted, and the area lacked an exhaust fan or any mechanical ventilation system, he said.During an inspection, officials from the Directorate of Industrial Safety and Health found that the pit did not conform to the company’s approved layout, the officer said. Since Kadam was the “occupier” of the premises, he was responsible for the installation, as no modifications could be made without his permission, the officer added.Police alleged that negligence in the matter led to the deaths of two workers and injuries to four others.
Article Summary: Schaeffler India chief executive officer and managing director Harsha Kadam was on Thursday formally arrested. He was later granted bail by a court in Vadgaon Maval. A senior police officer said seven accused had been arrested before Kadam in the case.

Article Title: Amravati Teachers’ Poll Today; 26 in fray for 1 MLC seat
Article Text:
Amravati:





The Amravati Division Teachers’ Constituency will go to polls on Friday to elect its representative to the Maharashtra Legislative Council.A total of 35,810 voters across Amravati, Akola, Yavatmal, Washim and Buldhana districts will decide the fate of 26 candidates. Voting will be held at 81 polling centres from 8 am to 4 pm through the preferential voting system.While it is officially a contest between Mahayuti and Maha Vikas Aghadi, the real fight on the ground is between Congress candidate Aditi Pohare and sitting MLC Kiran Sarnaik of Shiv Sena (Shinde faction).Sarnaik faces a tough challenge from within the ruling alliance. BJP rebels Sangita Shinde, Shekhar Bhoyar and Sumit Pawar, along with Shiv Sena rebel Shrikant Deshpande, are in the fray and are likely to split Mahayuti votes.Pohare, on the other hand, has the backing of her father and former minister Harshwardhan Deshmukh, who heads the Shri Shivaji Education Society — the largest educational institution network in Vidarbha. Her candidature has been further bolstered by Nagpur University Teachers’ Association (NUTA), which has included her in its panel of four candidates.Key issues dominating the campaign are restoration of the Old Pension Scheme (OPS) and demands of convent and unaided school teachers.In the 2020 election, Sarnaik had won as an Independent with 15,606 votes, including 6,095 first preference votes. He had defeated then sitting MLC Shrikant Deshpande, who polled 9,191 votes with 5,135 first preference votes as the Shiv Sena candidate. BJP’s Dr Nitin Dhande had finished a distant sixth.The constituency had recorded 81.10% turnout in 2020, with 30,918 of the total 38,129 voters exercising their franchise.
Article Summary: A total of 35,810 voters across Amravati, Akola, Yavatmal, Washim and Buldhana districts will decide the fate of 26 candidates. Voting will be held at 81 polling centres from 8 am to 4 pm through the preferential voting system.

Article Title: 13,608 graduates to vote at 26 polling stations in Gadchiroli

Gadchiroli

:





A total of 13,608 registered graduates will vote at 26 polling stations in Gadchiroli district on Friday for the Nagpur division graduates’ constituency election to the Maharashtra legislative council. Polling will be held from 8am to 4pm in eight talukas, while voters in four remote talukas will have to cast their votes by 3pm.District collector Avishyant Panda has appealed to all registered voters to exercise their franchise, particularly those in Etapalli, Bhamragad, Sironcha and Aheri, where polling will conclude an hour earlier following a revised notification by the Election Commission of India The district has 9,310 male and 4,298 female voters. Polling teams have been dispatched to their respective stations under police security.Gadchiroli taluka has the highest number of voters at 3,416 across six polling stations. Chamorshi has 2,125 voters at four stations, followed by Desaiganj with 1,839 and Armori with 1,756 across three stations each. Kurkheda has 1,288 voters at two stations, while Aheri has 1,120 at two stations.The remaining six talukas — Dhanora, Mulchera, Etapalli, Sironcha, Korchi and Bhamragad — have one polling station each.The Nagpur division constituency covers six districts — Nagpur, Wardha, Bhandara, Gondia, Chandrapur and Gadchiroli. Across the division, 2,55,603 voters are registered at 445 polling stations, with 38 candidates contesting the election.Registered government employees have been granted special casual leave to vote, while private-sector employees are to receive four hours’ leave.
Article Summary: 13,608 registered graduates will vote at 26 polling stations in Gadchiroli district on Friday for the Nagpur division graduates’ constituency election to the Maharashtra legislative council. Article Title: 21,742 Graduates to Vote at 41 polling stations in Wardha

Article Title: 864 bottles of liquor seized from house near Erode; man arrested
Article Text: ERODE: Police seized 864 bottles of Indian made foreign liquor (IMFL) from a house near Mylambadi in Erode district in the early hours of Thursday and arrested a man.Acting on a tip-off that bottles of liquor had been illegally stored for unauthorised sale, the Bhavani police conducted a raid at the house of K Govindaraj, 28, of Ammapalayam. Article Title: Temple archakar, man arrested for temple hundi theft cases in Tiruchendur
Article Text:
Tuticorin

:





Two men were accused in separate hundi theft cases at the Arulmigu Subramaniya Swamy Temple in Tiruchendur. While one accused, an archakar, was released on station bail, the other remanded in judicial custody despite both facing similar charges.According to police, the first case was registered at Tiruchendur Temple police station on October 16 under Section 305(c) (punishes theft committed in specific high-risk or sensitive locations) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) based on a complaint lodged by a temple official.The complaint alleged that Rs10,000 was stolen from a hundi located inside the temple premises between October 2 and 8.Police identified the accused as Muthan, 74, an archakar residing on South Car Street in Tiruchendur. During investigation, he was arrested at the police station. However, considering his advanced age and ill health, police released him on station bail.In a separate case, police registered a case on October 16 and arrested Murugan , 58, of Ariankuppam in Puducherry , for his involvement in a similar hundi theft of Rs10,000. He was remanded in judicial custody.
Article Summary: Two men were accused in separate hundi theft cases at the Arulmigu Subramaniya Swamy Temple in Tiruchendur. While one accused, an archakar, was released on station bail, the other remanded in judicial custody.

Article Title: Traffic affected on Salem-Madurai National Highway after trailer truck crashes near Rasipuram
Article Text: NAMAKKAL: Traffic was affected for more than an hour on the Salem-Madurai National Highway near Rasipuram in Namakkal district on Thursday afternoon after a trailer truck crashed while descending the Andagalur Gate flyover.No casualties or injuries were reported.The truck was carrying about 60 tonnes of steel angles from Maharashtra to Karur. An officer at the Rasipuram police station said the driver lost control of the vehicle while descending the flyover around 1.30pm. The truck hit a streetlight pole on the roadside. “The vehicle partially blocked the road, causing congestion and delays for motorists and commuters,” he said.Vehicles piled up for two kilometres on the NH. The Rasipuram police reached the spot after receiving information, regulated traffic and moved the truck to the roadside.Police registered a case and were investigating the circumstances leading to the crash.
Article Summary: Trailer truck crashes on Salem-Madurai National Highway near Rasipuram. Truck was carrying 60 tonnes of steel angles from Maharashtra to Karur. Driver lost control of the vehicle while descending the flyover. No casualties or injuries were reported.

Article Title: Sunilkumar criticises Pooram probe findings
Article Text:
CPI functionary V S Sunilkumar

Thrissur

:





CPI functionary V S Sunilkumar, who lost the Thrissur Lok Sabha election to BJP ’s Suresh Gopi , alleged on Thursday that the reported findings of the crime branch team probing the incidents that triggered a disruption of the 2024 Pooram festival were far from true.Sunilkumar said the findings, as reported in the media, appeared to provide an escape route for the real conspirators behind the incidents that had led to the suspension of Pooram festivities for several hours.Sunilkumar alleged that a political conspiracy had been hatched to sabotage Thrissur Pooram and claimed that the BJP and the RSS benefited from the disruption. He also alleged that then Thrissur district collector Krishna Teja too played a significant role in precipitating the crisis during the festival and added that the reported probe findings were silent on these aspects.Thiruvambady Devaswom office-bearers continued to criticise the findings, which reportedly named them as accused in the case.Devaswom secretary Gireesh Kumar said the office-bearers would meet the chief minister, the home minister and the devaswom minister to apprise them of what they considered shortcomings in the probe findings.
Article Summary: CPI functionary V S Sunilkumar lost the Thrissur Lok Sabha election to BJP ’s Suresh Gopi. He alleged that the reported findings of the crime branch team probing the incidents that triggered a disruption of the 2024 Pooram festival were far from true.

Article Title: Routine motor accident not ground for disqualification from temple panel, Kerala HC
Article Text:
Kochi

The high court has held that the mere registration of a routing vehicle accident criminal case that does not involve moral turpitude allegations, cannot be a valid ground for disqualifying a person from membership of a temple advisory committee.A bench of Justices V Raja Vijayaraghavan and K V Jayakumar was considering a petition by Radhakrishnan R of Karunagappally in Kollam, elected as a member of the temple advisory committee of Adinad Sakthikulangara Sree Durga Bhadra Bhagavathy Temple.The petitioner challenged the proceedings of the Travancore Devaswom Board sub group officer disqualifying him for the motorcycle accident case registered at the Karunagappally police on May 2, 2025.The bench noted that it was only a rash and negligent driving case. Article Title: Pay-off case: Kerala HC likely to hear former CM Pinarayi’s plea tomorrow
Article Text:
Pinarayi Vijayan

Kochi

:





The high court is likely to hear on Saturday, the appeals filed by former CM Pinarayi Vijayan and his relatives challenging a single bench order directing the registration of a vigilance case against them on the ED’s recommendation in connection with the alleged CMRL-Exalogic pay-off case.The Supreme Court had on Wednesday restored the appeals to the HC for fresh consideration after setting aside an earlier division bench order upholding the single bench directive. The apex court, in its order, had also stayed the vigilance probe into the allegations for 10 days. On Thursday, the appellants placed the Supreme Court order before the HC registry. The registry is expected to post the appeals before a different division bench.The litigation began when political activist K M Shajahan approached the HC challenging the state govt’s decision to constitute a special team to conduct a preliminary inquiry based on the ED’s recommendation to the state police chief to register the vigilance case.The single bench set aside the govt order constituting the special team and directed the registration of a vigilance case. Vijayan, his daughter Veena T, son-in-law and former minister P A Mohamed Riyas, and two others subsequently approached the division bench with appeals.As they were not parties to the original petition, they sought leave to challenge the order, contending that the single bench had passed it without hearing them.The division bench dismissed their leave applications and appeals, holding that an accused public servant has no right to be heard before an FIR is registered. They then approached the Supreme Court with special leave petitions, following which the apex court set aside the division bench’s order.
Article Summary: The high court is likely to hear on Saturday, the appeals filed by former CM Pinarayi Vijayan and his relatives. They are challenging a single bench order directing the registration of a vigilance case against them on the ED’s recommendation in connection with the alleged CMRL-Exalogic pay-off case.

Article Title: 10,470 voter roll entries found faulty in Pilibhit, action ordered against two EROs, operator
Article Text:
Of the 13,779 applications, 10,470 were approved and 3,309 rejected. All 10,470 approved entries were found irregular.





LUCKNOW: A detailed inquiry into electoral roll irregularities in Pilibhit assembly constituency has uncovered discrepancies in 10,470 voter records, prompting the Uttar Pradesh chief electoral officer (CEO) to order legal and departmental action against two Electoral Registration Officers (EROs) and a computer operator.The investigation was initiated following complaints that EPIC numbers assigned to registered voters were displaying the details of other electors.According to the inquiry report submitted by the Pilibhit district election officer, the Voter Registration Centre (VRC) operator entered 13,779 Form-8 applications for modifying voter details between May 31 and August 29, 2026.Of these, 4,717 entries were made until July 16, while another 9,062 were entered between July 17 and August 29. Significantly, no supporting application forms or documents for any of these entries were found in official records.Of the 13,779 applications, 10,470 were approved and 3,309 rejected. All 10,470 approved entries were found to be irregular.The CEO directed that legal proceedings be initiated against the operator and both EROs under Section 32 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950, and relevant provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.Orders were also issued to terminate the operator's services and initiate departmental proceedings against both EROs.The district administration has been directed to examine all Form-6 and Form-7 entries made between April 10 and October 21 and submit its findings within 24 hours. Corrections to the irregular entries are underway.
Article Summary: A detailed inquiry into electoral roll irregularities in Pilibhit assembly constituency has uncovered discrepancies in 10,470 voter records. Uttar Pradesh chief electoral officer (CEO) to order legal and departmental action against two Electoral Registration Officers (EROs) and a computer operator.

Article Title: Mumbai mayor’s office receives bomb threat email, 3 Delhi schools also targeted; searches underway
Article Text:
A bomb threat email was received at the Mumbai mayor's office, leading to a search which found nothing (Representative image)





MUMBAI: A bomb threat email was received at the Mumbai mayor’s office, prompting authorities to check the premises. However, nothing suspicious was found during the search.Meanwhile, three schools in Delhi allegedly received bomb threat emails on Friday morning, officials said.The threats prompted authorities to launch search operations at the schools. Officials are taking necessary measures to ensure the safety of the premises.
